come and Greetings
Dear RMIT Vietnam Parents and Families,
We are delighted to welcome you and your students to the RMIT
community.
Navigating university life can be both exciting and challenging for students,
and we understand it can be an anxious time for parents. RMIT is
committed to providing resources and services to ensure a safe and
supportive learning environment for all students.
RMIT values parents’ role in supporting children and believes education is
a partnership between students, families, and the university. As we
empower students to take charge of their success, your support is crucial in
recognising their potential, encouraging them to take ownership, embrace
challenges,

0ba508395da433c94e217f45699d265cd565777a.document:

recognising their potential, encouraging them to take ownership, embrace
challenges, and proactively seek support from the University when needed.
With this in mind, we encourage you to utilise the tailored resources
created by the RMIT Vietnam Family Connect team to foster students’
independence while providing families with the right information and
guidance to support students in being ready for what’s next.
We look forward to building a strong partnership with you and celebrating
your students' remarkable success.
Once again, welcome to the RMIT community.
Warm regards,
Professor Seng Kiat Kok

As parents and families, your support is invaluable in helping your student navigate their
university journey. While RMIT upholds strict privacy guidelines, you can still play a
crucial role by maintaining open communication with your student, encouraging their
independence, and guiding them on accessing relevant RMIT resources, services and
support.

students’ independence and resilience. By

decision-making abilities, and problem-

student for their future work and life.

Learning & Teaching
AAA Pedagogy
Digital teaching and
Blended learning
Our Triple A pedagogy (Active, Applied, and
Authentic), together with the University’s
Education Plan to 2028: Education for the Future
of Life and Work, has been scaled to ensure that
all learning is applied and all assessment is
authentic. The curriculum leverages AI and
emerging technologies and is aligned with industry
practices and tools to ensure relevance, currency,
and quality.
The student experience at RMIT includes
classroom learning, facilitated online and self-
directed learning, peer learning, industry field
trips, and

d2003c0b5206c9d793c0504960d0120aed130162.document:
learning, facilitated online and self-
directed learning, peer learning, industry field
trips, and guest speakers. Additionally, students
gain critical life and work skills through our
Personal Edge program.
Upon successful completion of their academic
journey, students receive a global RMIT degree.
All learning outcomes and assessments at RMIT
Vietnam are equivalent to those delivered at RMIT
Australia. Furthermore, we continuously monitor,
review and update our courses.
Blended learning is an important part of how
students learn at RMIT. This approach combines
the best of both worlds: engaging face-to-face
classes and flexible online learning. It helps
students build strong academic

classes and flexible online learning. It helps
students build strong academic skills while also
preparing them for the digital and professional
environments they will encounter in their future
careers.
RMIT’s  blended learning is designed to be
accessible, inclusive, and well-connected.

Results
Students can view their course results in myRMIT - the student administration platform. To
respect student privacy, results are accessed directly by students. Many families find it helpful
to discuss progress together, with students choosing how and when to share their progress.
Grades
Academic progress
Academic progress is the formal way RMIT supports s tudents who are not making satisfactory
progress in their program. In general, students who have failed 50% or more of their enrolled
course load in a compulsory semester or teaching period;

029ee756d9fbc02d9a4aebe6e2b7888295f5962c.document:
have failed 50% or more of their enrolled
course load in a compulsory semester or teaching period; and/or who have failed a course for a
second time may move into a status of academic at risk. If this happens, the student will be
advised by email that they are at risk of not meeting the academic requirements of their
program. Students who are identified as being at the final stage at risk might be excluded from
their program for a full academic year. At risk students are encouraged to seek support from
Student Academic Success - SAS (refer to page 15). More details can be found in the Academic
Progress section of the RMIT website.

rubric
An assessment rubric is a guide that shows how a student’s work will be evaluated. The
assessment rubric outlines what skills or tasks the student needs to show, what good
performance looks like and different achievement levels. In short, rubrics help students
understand exactly what is expected before they start an assignment.

Block-mode
courses
A block-mode course is a study format where students focus on one course at a time over a
short, intensive period. Each block typically lasts 4–6 weeks, with more frequent or longer
classes. This allows students to focus deeply on one subject and receive quicker feedback on
their progress.

Block-mode study can feel more intensive, but it helps students stay focused and manage
only one set of assessments at a time. Encouraging your child to plan ahead, keep up with
weekly tasks, and attend all classes will help them succeed.

missing important administrative deadlines,

Bảo hiểm y tế bắt buộc đối với sinh viên Việt Nam
Decree 105/2014/ND -CP, effective from 01 Jan 2015,  establishes a compulsory medical insurance
scheme for Vietnamese university students. It requires universities to collect the medical insurance fee
from Vietnamese students and pass that fee on to the Social Insurance Unit of the city where the campus
is located. More information is available at https://baohiemxahoi.gov.vn/Pages/default.aspx.
Nghị định 105/2014/NĐ-CP có hiệu lực từ ngày 01/01/2015 xây dựng khung bảo hiểm y tế bắt buộc dành
cho sinh viên Việt Nam đang học tại các trường đại

thu phí bảo hiểm y tế đối với sinh viên Việt Nam và chuyển phí đó về Văn phòng Bảo hiểm xã hội của

Notes about tuition fees
RMIT Vietnam has 3 semesters per year, in each semester you enrol into a maximum of 3 courses. The duration of programs is flexible and can be adapted on an individual basis upon enrolment.
Program fees are priced and invoiced in Vietnamese Dong (VND) by semester. Payments are made each semester, on a course-by-course basis.
Payments made in foreign currencies will be converted to Vietnamese Dong (VND)

2312080bccc92b2a3c62488c10f1cae609cb8ca4.document:
rse-by-course basis.
Payments made in foreign currencies will be converted to Vietnamese Dong (VND) based on the applicable exchange rate on the transaction date. Any currency conversion fees and related bank charges will be borne by the student.
Online payment via
myRMIT
is the preferred payment method, as it offers secure transactions, automatic confirmation, and faster processing.
Medical Insurance is compulsory for international students. Suitable medical insurance will be arranged by RMIT Vietnam on behalf of the student. Should an international student choose to arrange their own medical insurance, evidence of this must be provided before the semester begins.
The National Medical

5b428735a7335adb9937c087fa23e3c867ffa0b0.document:
dical insurance, evidence of this must be provided before the semester begins.
The National Medical Insurance Fee is paid by all Vietnamese university students in Vietnam. The level of the fee is related to the minimum wage in Vietnam.
Medical insurance fees are subject to change without notice.

How do I know if I am a new (commencing) or continuing (returning) student?
Different fee groups apply for new (commencing) and continuing (returning) students in each year. Please see definition below, to be read in conjunction with the Fee Group definitions:
New (Commencing) students:
Never enrolled into any program at RMIT Vietnam; or
Return after a period of no enrolment; or
EU: returning after a gap of 6 months or more
Academic program: 1 semester gap without a valid enrolment status (Enrolled, LOA) except for intake unavailability reason
Completed a Bachelor, Master, or PhD

a767a7f88af623fba7738e47b45bd0b6ad7870f2.document:
status (Enrolled, LOA) except for intake unavailability reason
Completed a Bachelor, Master, or PhD program and enrol in another program; or
Completed a Foundation Studies program and articulate to another program; or
Completed an English language program and enrol in another program; or
For example:
Completed Teen program and enrol in EU program; or
Completed a UniStart Academic or Graduate Certificate without a package offer, and enrol in another program
Not otherwise classified as a continuing (returning) student.
Continuing (Returning) students:
Have remained continuously enrolled or are on an approved LOA; or
Transferring to another program without completing the previous program while

bd4eedb98871b1a8ce2f230abd460f85e3d80bfb.document:
n an approved LOA; or
Transferring to another program without completing the previous program while remain continuous enrolment or on an approved LOA; or
Completed UniStart Academic or Graduate Certificate as part of a package offer, and articulate to another program without any semester gap or with a semester gap due to intake unavailability.
My tuition fee has increased this semester. Why?
Annual fee adjustments have been applied in line with the Consumer Price Index and changes in operating costs, enabling us to continue to improve our quality.
When will I receive my tuition debit note for the new semester?
A debit note is emailed to students on Friday before the new semester starts.
If

the new semester?

View your
Financial Account
via
myRMIT
on the day after enrolment changes
Received updated debit notes on every Wednesday in the semester
Do I get a receipt or confirmation of payment?
If you need to confirm payment, you can check via the Financial Account tile in
myRMIT
, or ask a Student Connect advisor; however, payments may take up to three days to clear.
When is the deadline for payment?
The Payment deadline for tuition fees is on Friday in Week 3 of each semester, except for Block courses and Intensive

ee44e8e959958686e315bae8b207388cf5ac8061.document:
ne for tuition fees is on Friday in Week 3 of each semester, except for Block courses and Intensive PostGrads courses as follows:
Block course: the deadline for payment is on Friday of the first week of the block course.
Intensive PostGrads course: the deadline for payment is on the day before the course's start date.
What happens if I miss the tuition payment deadline?
Failure to pay all fees and charges by the Payment Date may result in a student being withdrawn from all enrolled courses and placed on administrative Cancellation unless exceptional circumstances apply, and a timely application is lodged and approved.
The penalty will affect students whose have overdue amount is as follows:

eba7dd2f77178e4e9af083c76d11803b69686ebc.document:
n is lodged and approved.
The penalty will affect students whose have overdue amount is as follows:
Standard course: greater than or equal to 5 million VND
Block course and Intensive Postgrad course: greater than or equal to 1 million VND
The penalties for withdrawal will be determined based on the corresponding timeline of the courses.
You will receive an updated tuition fee debit note that reverses course fees. However, library and other fees will not be reversed.
Can I seek an extension of payment?
Extensions are permitted in specific circumstances.
You can read more here
.

You can pay tuition fees via the Financial Account tile in
myRMIT
, or by bank

pay my tuition fees?
You can pay tuition fees via the Financial Account tile in
myRMIT
, or by bank transfer or by credit card. Visit
this link
for more details regarding payment methods.
My debit note/my outstanding balance has a negative number. What does it mean?
When a number is negative, for example -2,000,000 VND, it means that amount is in credit or being reversed from an earlier debit note or a waiver.
If your total balance is in credit, you may be eligible for a refund or re-credit; any amount in credit can be used to offset against future fees.
What is the deadline for adding/dropping courses without penalty?
By Friday in Week 4 to avoid incurring full fees.
By Friday in Week 8 to

121f845f14f4e28393797e363bab63de849d82b6.document:
g courses without penalty?
By Friday in Week 4 to avoid incurring full fees.
By Friday in Week 8 to avoid avoid incurring full fees and academic penalty of NN grade (Fail).
Except for Block courses and Intensive PostGrads courses as follows:
Block course:
Drop by the Friday of Week 2 to avoid incurring full fees.
Drop by the Friday of Week 3 to avoid incurring full fees and academic penalties.
PostGrad intensive course:
Drop on the first intensive day to avoid incurring full fees.
Drop by the second intensive day to avoid incurring full fees and academic penalties.
What if I am placed on administrative Cancellation due to Unpaid Fee and would like to come back to study?
You are allowed to

303f30e767989ae765739333782878afd5b0436e.document:
inistrative Cancellation due to Unpaid Fee and would like to come back to study?
You are allowed to come back to study the following semester, subject to the terms and conditions outlined in
the Student Fees and Charges Guide
(PDF, 803KB, 65p). Any outstanding debt must be paid before the student can successfully re-apply for entry into RMIT Vietnam or another campus of RMIT University.
I am going to study at RMIT next semester; however I have to cancel my enrolment. Can I get a refund on my deposit?
The deposit of 20 million VND is generally non-refundable and will only be refunded if you are given a conditional offer but fail to meet the conditions of that offer, OR if the University

f8e0d7083cc46e3d1b7aefb4ce2fa14c01653c27.document:
u are given a conditional offer but fail to meet the conditions of that offer, OR if the University cancels an intake into a program.
I have a credit in my RMIT account but I do not want to apply for a refund as I am continuing to study. Can I use my credit for future fees?
Yes. The amount you have will be kept in credit and deducted from future tuition fees.
I am enrolled in courses and have paid my tuition fees. However, due to my sickness, I cannot study this semester and the deadline of LOA submission has passed. Can I get a refund of my fee or a re-credit for a future semester?
You may qualify for a Remission of Debt. Contact Student Connect for instructions on how to submit a

0f1aca06f40e9b69964e51e0865276b4156cc9e4.document:
ou may qualify for a Remission of Debt. Contact Student Connect for instructions on how to submit a remission of debt form and supporting documents.
Do I have to pay a medical insurance fee?
The medical insurance fee is compulsory for both local and international students studying at RMIT Vietnam. Should students choose to arrange their own medical insurance, evidence of insurance must be provided at least 10 days before a semester starts. Students can apply for an insurance waiver via
myRMIT
.
More information can be found on the
Health Insurance
page.

What is the VCB gift card?
The VietcomBank (VCB) Gift Card is issued on SGS campus by VCB at the cashier counter: Level 1, Building 2. It is only offered to students who are ineligible to open a bank account or first-time visitors to campus.
I am only on campus as a visitor, do I still need to use a VCB Gift Card?
It is not required to have a Gift Card to use services if you already have other bank cards or use e-wallets.
How do I obtain a VCB Gift Card / where on campus in SGS, Hanoi and Danang can I purchase one?

What happens if I have left over credit on my VCB Gift Card, can it be refunded to me?
The balance on this card is not eligible for cashback. The value of the card is VND 100,000 and you can use it in RMIT campuses in 3 years from the issuance date.
